**Subject: The building on Saint-Hubert**

Denis,

I have been trying to write this without letting my anger do all the talking. I am furious with you, but you are my brother, and I don’t want this to become something we can never come back from.

On Thursday morning, at six, I was shaping baguettes when a photographer from the agency came into my shop. He told me you had said I was okay with him being there. I had no idea what he was talking about. Karine had to calm me down.

That is how I learned you were putting Papa’s building on the market. Not from you. From a stranger with a camera, standing in my bakery. Afterwards I found the listing on Centris, asking $1,150,000.

Denis, how could you do this without calling me?

After Maman’s funeral, you told me, “No rush, we decide together.” I have not forgotten those words. Together. Since the estate was settled in August, the building has been half yours and half mine. Whatever you want to do with your half, you cannot honestly think that sending an agent and a photographer into my shop is deciding together.

I told you in September, on the phone, that I wanted to buy your half. The caisse has pre-approved me for $410,000. You knew I was interested. If that amount is not enough for you, then tell me. We can talk about the price and how to find something fair. But you did not even give me that conversation before putting the building up for sale.

Papa bought the building on rue Saint-Hubert in 1979. You know every corner of it as well as I do: the bakery downstairs and the two apartments upstairs. Do you remember when Papa let you sleep in the room at the back where we kept the flour sacks? You loved it in there. I can still see you making yourself comfortable as if it were your own little apartment.

I know memories alone do not pay the bills, and I am not asking you to pretend the building has no value. But please don’t dismiss me as sentimental. This is business for me too. My bakery has been there for 31 years. I have six employees who depend on this place for their work, and customers who have been coming through the door for years. This is not just an address I can easily replace.

I have paid $2,400 a month in rent to the estate and have never been late once. In 2019, I paid $38,000 myself for the new roof. I did that because the building needed it and because I have always taken my responsibilities there seriously. I need you to take those things seriously too when we talk about what happens next.

My lease ends on April 30, 2027. I am frightened about what a sale could mean. A developer might want to tear the building down or turn it into condos. A new owner could put the rent up beyond what I can afford. I don’t know what a buyer would do, but I know I cannot survive if the rent doubles. You are making a decision that could put my livelihood, my employees’ jobs, and everything we have built at risk.

And I keep coming back to that photographer. You told him I was okay with him coming in when you had not even asked me. I was working, minding my own business, and suddenly a stranger knew more about your plans for our building than I did. I felt blindsided and deeply disrespected. I am angry that you used an agent instead of picking up the phone yourself. It felt cowardly, Denis. You should have spoken to me.

I am asking you to take the building off the market this week so we can sit down and discuss it properly. At the very least, give me the first opportunity to buy your half before you go any further with a sale. I want us to find out what the building is worth, talk honestly about the numbers, including the roof, and see whether we can reach an agreement that is fair to both of us. I am not asking you to give me anything for free. I am asking you to deal with me directly and give me a real chance.

Please call me this week. I want to hear from you, not receive a text from your wife. I know this is difficult to talk about, but it needs to be a conversation between the two of us.

I miss Maman, and I know you do too. We have both had a difficult year. That does not excuse what happened, but it is one more reason I don’t want us to let this destroy our relationship. Papa’s building matters to me, the bakery matters to me, and you matter to me too, even when I am this angry with you.

Please call me, Denis. Let’s keep our word to each other and decide together.

Your sister
